name: Theory of Computation
description: Finite automata and regular languages, context-free grammars and pushdown automata, Turing machines and decidability.

nodes.name: Finite automata
nodes.desc: Alphabets, strings and languages; DFAs and designing a DFA for a language.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define alphabets, strings and languages and design DFAs that accept a given language.

nodes.name: NFAs
nodes.desc: Nondeterminism, epsilon moves and converting an NFA to a DFA with the subset construction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design NFAs with epsilon moves and convert them to equivalent DFAs using the subset construction.

nodes.name: DFA minimisation
nodes.desc: Minimising DFAs, distinguishable states and the Myhill–Nerode theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to minimise a DFA by merging equivalent states and use the Myhill-Nerode theorem to bound state counts.

nodes.name: Product automata
nodes.desc: Combining DFAs for intersection and union, and counting strings or states.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build product automata for union and intersection and count states or accepted strings.
topics: Counting accepted strings of a length

nodes.name: Regular expressions
nodes.desc: Regular expressions, equivalence with finite automata and state elimination.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write regular expressions for languages and convert between regular expressions and finite automata.
topics: Thompson's construction from regex to NFA
State elimination from DFA to regex

nodes.name: Regular languages
nodes.desc: Recognising regular languages and reasoning about which languages are regular.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide whether a language is regular by reasoning about finite memory and known constructions.

nodes.name: Closure properties
nodes.desc: Closure of regular languages under union, intersection, complement, reversal, homomorphism and quotient.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the closure properties of regular languages to prove languages regular or non-regular.

nodes.name: Pumping lemma
nodes.desc: Proving languages non-regular with the pumping lemma.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove that languages are not regular using the pumping lemma as an adversarial game.

nodes.name: Language operations
nodes.desc: Prefix, suffix, substring, reversal, quotient and homomorphism applied to regular languages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply prefix, suffix, substring, reversal, quotient and homomorphism operations to regular languages.

nodes.name: Context-free grammars
nodes.desc: Grammars, derivations and parse trees; working out the language a grammar generates.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write context-free grammars, build derivations and parse trees and determine the language a grammar generates.
topics: Finding the language of a grammar

nodes.name: Regular grammars
nodes.desc: Left- and right-linear grammars and converting between them and finite automata.
nodes.summary: You will be able to convert between left- and right-linear grammars and finite automata.
topics: Converting a DFA to a right-linear grammar
Converting a grammar to an NFA

nodes.name: Ambiguity
nodes.desc: Ambiguous grammars and inherently ambiguous languages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to show that a grammar is ambiguous, remove ambiguity where possible and recognise inherently ambiguous languages.

nodes.name: Normal forms
nodes.desc: Chomsky and Greibach normal forms and derivation lengths in CNF.
nodes.summary: You will be able to convert grammars to Chomsky and Greibach normal form and compute derivation lengths in CNF.

nodes.name: Pushdown automata
nodes.desc: PDAs, acceptance by final state and empty stack, and equivalence with CFGs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design pushdown automata and show their equivalence with context-free grammars.

nodes.name: DPDAs & DCFLs
nodes.desc: Deterministic PDAs and deterministic context-free languages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify deterministic PDAs and deterministic context-free languages and how they differ from general CFLs.

nodes.name: CFL closure
nodes.desc: Closure and non-closure of CFLs and DCFLs, including intersection with regular languages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to determine closure and non-closure of CFLs and DCFLs, including intersection with regular languages.

nodes.name: Pumping for CFLs
nodes.desc: Proving languages not context-free with the CFL pumping lemma.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove that languages are not context-free with the pumping lemma for context-free languages.
topics: Statement of the CFL pumping lemma

nodes.name: Turing machines
nodes.desc: Turing machines, variants and their equivalence, enumerators and the Church–Turing thesis.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design Turing machines, compare their variants and explain the Church-Turing thesis.

nodes.name: Recursive & RE sets
nodes.desc: Recursive and recursively enumerable languages and their closure properties.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish recursive and recursively enumerable languages and apply their closure properties.
topics: L and its complement both RE

nodes.name: Chomsky hierarchy
nodes.desc: Regular, context-free, context-sensitive and RE languages, and placing a language in the hierarchy.
nodes.summary: You will be able to place a language in the Chomsky hierarchy and relate each level to its grammar and machine model.

nodes.name: Decidability
nodes.desc: Decidable and undecidable problems about automata, grammars and Turing machines.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide which problems about automata, grammars and Turing machines are decidable.

nodes.name: Halting & reductions
nodes.desc: The halting problem, reductions and Rice's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove undecidability through the halting problem, many-one reductions and Rice's theorem.

nodes.name: Countability
nodes.desc: Countable and uncountable sets and diagonalisation: why some languages are not RE.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify sets as countable or uncountable and use diagonalisation to show some languages are not RE.
topics: A language that is not RE
